findings.summary: Ridgeline-FT did not significantly differ from Plainweave-FT in pass@1 on Quillbench (mean 46.1% vs 45.6%; paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p=0.36, 95% CI [-0.75, 1.79] percentage points).
findings.scope: Quillbench, 420 Python problems, greedy decoding, 8 paired seeds, pass@1 metric
findings.caveats: Non-significant difference is not evidence of equivalence; CI includes both negative and positive values.

findings.summary: Ridgeline-FT significantly outperformed Plainweave-FT in compile rate on Quillbench (mean 93.1% vs 90.4%; paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0087, 95% CI [1.19, 4.35] percentage points).
findings.scope: Quillbench, 420 Python problems, greedy decoding, 8 paired seeds, compile rate metric
findings.caveats: Secondary endpoint; significance controlled across two endpoints via Holm–Bonferroni.

findings.summary: Both fine-tuned recipes improved pass@1 and compile rate over the base Fernleaf-1.3B model (pass@1: 46.1% and 45.6% vs 31.4%; compile: 93.1% and 90.4% vs 84.0%).
findings.scope: Quillbench, 420 Python problems, greedy decoding, base model single run vs fine-tuned 8-seed means
findings.caveats: Base model is a single deterministic run; no statistical test reported for these comparisons.

sentences.text: On Quillbench, Ridgeline-FT did not significantly differ from Plainweave-FT in pass@1 (46.1% ± 1.8% vs 45.6% ± 1.7%; paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p = 0.36, 95% CI [-0.75, 1.79] percentage points).
However, Ridgeline-FT significantly outperformed Plainweave-FT in compile rate (93.1% ± 1.3% vs 90.4% ± 1.8%; paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0087, 95% CI [1.19, 4.35] percentage points).
Both fine-tuned recipes improved pass@1 and compile rate over the base Fernleaf-1.3B model (pass@1: 46.1% and 45.6% vs 31.4%; compile: 93.1% and 90.4% vs 84.0%).
